title: Insurance Programme
summary: Every insurance question used to be a request to a colleague. Fifteen years of records sat in three places, linked only by reference number. I linked them once, then answered the recurring questions with dashboards and the rest with an assistant that cites its sources.

sections.heading: The problem
paragraphs: Fifteen years of records in three places, linked only by reference number: no database, no data governance, nothing for AI to analyse. The Group's own programme and the dealer programme shared the problem.

sections.heading: Link once, answer two ways
paragraphs: Open a class and its policies and claims come with it, each policy with its PDF attached. Both programmes sit on the same structure.
The questions asked every month became dashboards — premium by class, broker share, trend, loss ratio — so the fixed answers never depend on a model. Everything beyond them goes to the assistant.

sections.heading: The assistant
paragraphs: Three choices keep its answers reliable.
bullets: Scope — answers only from the tables and the policy documents in them; if the answer is not there, it says so
Sources — every answer cites where it came from; legal points cite references I specified, for a specialist to confirm
Tools — reads the policy PDFs, draws its own charts, runs the numbers: ask where a loss ratio is heading and it fits the trend on the years on record

sections.heading: On the phone
paragraphs: The same system, laid out for the phone with the assistant first — for managers out without a laptop.

sections.heading: From dashboard to report
paragraphs: To share a view, pick a year, a range and the sections. Figures come from the database, the narrative from a language model that only explains the charts it is given, the layout from a script — a Word file, ready to edit. The model is DeepSeek V4 Flash: a low-stakes task gets an inexpensive one.

sections.heading: About the demo
paragraphs: The employer is not named. Aggregates are synthetic and badged as such; record-level fields show as "Redacted" bars; the assistant is a visual replica and says so. Rebuilt in React and NestJS for the public demo.
